title: Waste segregation and environmental controls
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and salvage after a fire or smoke event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a fire-damaged building, release it, or certify it as safe.
learningOutcomes: Characterise waste before moving it, and refer suspect streams to specialist segregation and licensed handling.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to characterise fire-damaged waste before it is moved, and how to route suspect streams to specialist or licensed handling. It does not authorise anyone to transport, store or dispose of waste. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Waste segregation and environmental controls
instruction.body: Characterise waste before anyone moves it. Suspected asbestos, chemical containers, batteries and other hazardous residues may need specialist segregation and licensed handling. Record who will transport and who will receive each waste stream. Never classify unknown contaminated waste as general rubbish by default. A customer who asks cleaners to place charred debris and unknown insulation in normal bins is asking for something that must be refused. In training, complete a simulated waste-transfer log and identify the streams that need confirmation from the local authority or a specialist.

procedure: Stop before moving any debris, insulation or container.
Characterise each stream as far as possible: suspected asbestos, chemical containers, batteries, charred material and general debris.
Keep suspect streams separate, labelled and contained.
Record who will transport and who will receive each stream.
Confirm the disposal route in writing with the authority or a specialist. Do not use general waste for any suspect stream.
Complete the transfer log before any stream leaves the site.

workedExamples.situation: The customer asks cleaners to place charred debris and unknown insulation in the normal bins.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must be done with the waste?
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse the general-bin route. Characterise the waste, identify the streams that need specialist or licensed handling, and record the transport and receiving parties.

workedExamples.situation: A skip is due to be filled with debris from a burned kitchen, and the crew has not yet seen the insulation.
workedExamples.reasoning: Hold the skip. Characterise the streams first, and confirm the route in writing before anything is loaded.

equipmentAndPpe: Labelled containers and a transfer log, handled only by authorised people.
Gloves and eye protection for handling, selected from the hazard assessment.

commonErrors.error: Putting charred debris or unknown insulation into general bins.
commonErrors.prevention: Characterise the waste and route suspect streams to specialist segregation and licensed handling.

commonErrors.error: Mixing suspect and general streams into one skip.
Filling a skip before the waste is characterised.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold until the stream is assessed and the route is confirmed in writing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not authorise transport, storage or disposal of waste. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
In Victoria, WorkSafe's bushfire guidance points to the Environment Protection Authority for waste transport and disposal.
Where asbestos is confirmed, the Victorian and Western Australian guidance both call for a licensed asbestos removalist.

qualityStandard: The learner characterises waste before moving it and separates suspect streams.
The learner names the transporter and the receiver for each stream.
documentationEvidence: Residue and waste decision register: description, suspected hazard, classification owner, receiver, transport permission and retained evidence.
summary: Suspect streams go to specialist or licensed routes.

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks cleaners to place charred debris and unknown insulation in normal bins. What is correct?
options: Agree, because the bins are collected every week and the waste will be removed with the household rubbish
Refuse. Characterise the waste and route suspect streams to specialist segregation and licensed handling.
Agree if the customer signs for it, since the customer takes responsibility for the waste after it leaves

officialReferences.title: Bushfire recovery: asbestos clean-up
officialReferences.pageDate: Reviewed on 04/05/2023 (4 May 2023); no later date shown
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Friable post-bushfire asbestos clean-up must be done by a Class A (friable) licence holder or an employee directly engaged by one; non-friable clean-up can be done by a Class B (non-friable) licence holder or an employee directly engaged by one. Fire can break down non-friable asbestos into friable material. A documented site risk assessment by a competent person is required before make-safe or clean-up work. If asbestos is inaccessible or its condition is uncertain, treat it as friable. Work must stop immediately if asbestos is found or suspected. Signs and barricades stay in place until an independent person inspects the site and issues a clearance certificate. Waste transport and disposal is directed to the Environment Protection Authority. Victorian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Asbestos safety after an emergency or disaster
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Do not enter a property until authorities confirm it is safe. Avoid spreading ash or moving debris by sweeping or vacuuming. Never use high-pressure sprays; dampen ash and debris lightly to limit dust. Wear a P2 face mask and protective clothing such as sturdy boots and gloves, even if unsure whether asbestos is present. Contact a competent person or licensed asbestos assessor before clean-up starts. If asbestos is confirmed, a licensed asbestos removalist carries out the clean-up. Urgent removal: notify WorkSafe and submit the notification within 24 hours. Emergency work still requires a clearance. WA guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: Fire-scene release, structural and utility isolation, asbestos assessment and removal, and some waste handling are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people, and may be controlled by fire investigators, the police, structural engineers, utilities or the building owner. Insurer and owner permission do not replace a release from the authority that controls the site. Where that authority is not identified, do not proceed.

stopWorkAndReferral: Stop and refer when waste would be classified as general rubbish without characterisation.
A stop-work decision is correct, so record it and restart only once the competent party confirms the scope in writing.
